title: Photo 197 · 콜로설 · 마키에 · 무릎 꿇기 정면 (한쪽 무릎) · 남아시아 20대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless deep-charcoal backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult South Asian woman in her late 20s, rich warm brown skin tone with golden undertones, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, long finger waves falling past her shoulders, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears large teardrop studs and has square nails with a glass-like shine.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so wide that her hips are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is young and firm for its size, each fold holding a taut rounded shape. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, settles and presses down onto the thighs beneath it.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a smooth taut surface with natural creases and shadow only where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Japanese maki-e lacquer style — glossy black lacquer with sprinkled gold powder shading into flowing autumn grasses, chrysanthemums, plum branches and full moons, bold gold bands following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs, a scattered gold-flake ground filling the space between every motif. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Kneeling on one knee on the platform facing the camera, one shin and foot folded back beneath her with that thigh lying flat, the other knee raised in front of her with the foot planted flat on the platform, the great mass of her middle settling down over the flat thigh on one side and pressing against the raised thigh on the other, her back straight, her hands resting on her thighs with her arms held clear of her body so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head level and facing the lens, full body head to feet filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme gold platform stiletto sandals with double ankle straps, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the gold powder glittering, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
